_meta.policy: Identified, marked, never silently approximated. An item with blocks_execution=true refuses to run until an explicit operationalisation is recorded in the run configuration and copied into the run manifest (ADV-M18-R01, ADV-M18-C03).

execution_model_parameters.name: setup_expiry_bars
execution_model_parameters.why: No specification states how long a partially formed setup stays live. Without a bound, a latched liquidity event that never produced displacement would block the machine for the rest of the sample.
execution_model_parameters.status: execution-model research parameter, not a rule from the source (ADV-M18-C03); required, no default; recorded in the run manifest.

execution_model_parameters.name: intrabar_policy
execution_model_parameters.why: When a bar's range contains both the stop and a target, the source cannot say which came first.
execution_model_parameters.status: declared choice ('stop_first' or 'target_first'), recorded in the run manifest.

execution_model_parameters.name: latch supersession
execution_model_parameters.why: A pending setup is abandoned when the market prints a different first event (a different origin pool, or a different sweep of it).
execution_model_parameters.status: fixed execution-model rule, documented in DSL_SPEC.md; it removes no condition the source states.

source.text: If the selected Kill Zone window closes without a qualifying setup, no trade is the correct and disciplined outcome. A day where the plan correctly identified no qualifying setup, and no trade was forced, is recorded as a process success, not a wasted day.

items.explanation: 'No trade' is the default outcome of the engine, and recording it as a process success is a journaling instruction.
items.resolution: Record it in the run report; it is not evaluated by the engine.

source.text: Step 10b — market entry once price reaches the zone AND shows an additional LTF confirmation (e.g. 1-minute bullish MSS or a rejection candle).

items.element: 'rejection candle' as an alternative lower-timeframe confirmation

items.resolution: Select ltf_confirmation_signal = 'ltf_mss', or supply a definition and record it as a research operationalisation (ADV-M18-C03).

source.text: When time-based expectations fail (expected kill zone produces no liquidity event and no displacement; expansion begins in a dead zone and is immediately reversed; a higher-timeframe opposing force overrides the daily time map), require a re-check of the liquidity and structural narrative, not a forced trade in the next window. Do not trade every kill zone regardless of whether a delivery narrative is active. Do not elevate a lower-timeframe signal appearing outside any relevant kill zone to the same quality as an in-window signal. Do not assume that if London did nothing, New York must reverse -- the higher-timeframe narrative still governs.

source.text: The OTE concept should be de-emphasised or ignored when: (1) no clear displacement has occurred after a liquidity event; (2) the higher-timeframe narrative is ambiguous or conflicting; (3) price is still inside a tight consolidation with no expansion leg to measure; (4) the calculated OTE falls on the wrong side of dealing-range equilibrium relative to the intended direction; (5) the only available PD arrays inside the zone have already been mitigated; (6) session timing is unfavourable (e.g. attempting a full OTE model in a low-volatility period with no kill-zone alignment); (7) the trader is forcing a Fibonacci on a leg that is not the institutional expansion.

items.explanation: Clauses 1, 2 and 4 are enforced by the sequence (displacement required, bias gate, premium/discount filter); clauses 3 and 6 ('tight consolidation', 'low volatility with no kill-zone alignment') have no price test in the source.
items.resolution: Record it in the run report; it is not evaluated by the engine.
items.effect_if_unenforced: The run may include trades the specification would have stood aside from; reported selectivity is therefore an upper bound.

source.text: Overtrading = taking trades that fail the model-selection filters (Module 15) or the pre-entry checklist (Module 16), usually from feeling the need to be in the market -- includes trading outside the authorised session window, trading when bias is unclear, trading lower-quality arrays, and adding risk after the daily risk ceiling has been reached. When the model shortlist is empty, the correct action is zero trades. Revenge trading = attempting to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade not authorised by the narrative and filters, almost always accompanied by increased size or loosened invalidation -- after a loss, return to the narrative stack and selection procedure; if invalidated or no sequence appears, take no further risk (daily loss limit is the final backstop). Do not use fixed-pip stops that ignore the array and structure. Do not reject a high-quality narrative solely because R:R is below an arbitrary number. Do not widen the stop after entry 'to give it room.' Do not continue trading after the daily loss limit has been hit. Do not revenge-size the next trade after a loss. Do not treat 'I need to make back the loss' as a valid reason to select a model. Do not ignore narrative invalidation because the trade is still open and 'might come back.'

items.explanation: Overtrading is a behavioural failure, not a market condition.
items.resolution: Record it in the run report; it is not evaluated by the engine.

items.effect_if_unenforced: Breakers formed from low-quality order blocks are included; the population is broader than the specification intends.

source.text: High-impact scheduled news can produce non-structural spikes that violate otherwise sound stops. Practice: reduce size, widen stops only with a corresponding size reduction, or stand aside around the event window when the narrative does not explicitly depend on the release. When volatility expands beyond the structural assumptions of the setup, capital preservation is the priority -- closing or reducing the position is preferable to hoping the narrative reasserts itself immediately.

items.explanation: The listed condition is a rule object, not a no-trade object, and it depends on an economic calendar the specification does not define or bound.
